title: DIY vs Contractor Hour Mix
dataSources: Renovation tasks (`reno:task`), budget and receipts (`reno:budget`), material orders (`reno:material`), inspections (`reno:inspection`), contractor logs (`reno:contractor`).
app: Home-renovation project management — task boards (Trello, Notion), budget and receipt trackers, material orders, and inspection / permit logs — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=reno:contractor
| stats sum(eval(if(worker_type="diy",hours_worked,0))) as diy_hours, sum(eval(if(worker_type="contractor",hours_worked,0))) as contractor_hours by project_phase
| eval diy_share_pct=round(100*diy_hours/(diy_hours+contractor_hours),1)
| sort - diy_share_pct
description: Shows which phases are mostly homeowner effort versus contracted labor.
value: Hour mix helps explain budget savings, fatigue, and why some phases slip more than others.
implementation: Tag work logs by worker type and project phase; compute DIY share percentage for each phase.
visualization: Stacked bar chart of DIY versus contractor hours by phase.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces how much of each project phase is being carried by you versus paid tradespeople.
